ing: soaked and ground, or 1 tbsp chili flakes
st: Blend the garlic, chili, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and pepper with [[3 tbsp]] vinegar and [[3 tbsp]] oil to make a thick paste.
Rub the paste all over the lamb pieces, working it into every crevice.
Cover and marinate the lamb in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or overnight for deeper flavor.
Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C). If using banana leaves, hold them briefly over a flame or dip in hot water to soften them.
Wrap the lamb tightly in two layers of banana leaves, or in parchment and then foil, and tie or seal so no steam escapes.
Place the bundle in a deep roasting pan and cover the pan tightly with foil.
Bake for 5 hours until the lamb is very tender and pulls apart easily. Check that it has reached at least 145°F (63°C), though it should be far beyond that when done.
Rest the bundle for 15 minutes, then unwrap carefully, as hot steam will escape.
Serve the pulled lamb with rice and the juices from the packet.
Soak the rinsed rice in cold water for [[20 minutes]] while you prepare the rest, then drain.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onions for 10 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic, cinnamon stick, cardamom, cumin, turmeric and pepper and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and brown on all sides for about 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and dried limes and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Pour in [[4 cups]] broth and [[2 tsp]] salt, bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken and set it aside. Measure the broth in the pot; you want about [[4 cups]], so add water if short.
Add the drained rice to the pot, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover tightly and cook for 18 minutes.
Meanwhile, broil or pan-fry the chicken for 5 minutes until the skin is browned.
Fluff the rice, rest it for 5 minutes, and serve topped with the chicken.

ing: or other firm white fish such as mahi-mahi
st: Mix the minced garlic, [[1 tsp]] cumin, turmeric, paprika, [[1 tsp]] salt, pepper, the juice of 2 lemons and [[2 tbsp]] oil into a marinade.
Coat the fish in the marinade and let it sit for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the sliced onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the rinsed rice, [[1 tsp]] cumin and [[1 tsp]] salt and toast for 1 minute.
Add [[3.5 cups]] water, bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low and cook for 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Heat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat, or heat the broiler.
Grill the fish for 4 to 5 minutes per side until opaque and flaking easily, reaching 145°F (63°C).
Fluff the rice and serve the fish on top with lemon wedges.

ing: pearled wheat or whole wheat berries
st: Drain the soaked wheat and rinse it well under cold water.
Put the wheat, chicken, onion, [[8 cups]] water and [[2 tsp]] salt in a large heavy pot and bring to a boil.
Skim off any foam, then cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour, until the chicken is cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chicken, let it cool slightly, then shred the meat and discard the bones. Remove the onion.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot and continue to cook, stirring often, for 1 hour 30 minutes until the wheat breaks down.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter and the pepper. Mash and beat the mixture with a wooden spoon or potato masher for 5 minutes until thick and smooth like porridge.
Add a splash of hot water if it is too thick.
Melt the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter and stir in the cinnamon and cardamom.
Spoon the harees into bowls and drizzle with the spiced butter.

ing: crumbled, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
st: Grease a shallow dish or tray with ghee and set aside.
Whisk the cornstarch with [[2 cups]] cold water until completely smooth with no lumps.
In a heavy nonstick pot, combine the sugar and [[2 cups]] water and heat until the sugar dissolves.
Pour in the cornstarch mixture slowly, stirring constantly, and cook over medium-low heat until it starts to thicken and turn glossy.
Add the ghee a few tablespoons at a time, stirring well after each addition so it blends in.
Keep stirring for 45 to 60 minutes until the mixture turns dark amber, pulls away from the pot and is very thick.
Stir in the saffron and its water, [[2 tbsp]] rosewater, cardamom, nutmeg and half of the nuts.
Pour into the greased dish, smooth the top and scatter the remaining nuts on top.
Let it cool completely for at least 1 hour, then cut into squares.
Mix the garlic, chili, vinegar, cumin, tamarind paste, turmeric, salt, pepper and [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large bowl.
Add the beef cubes and toss until every piece is coated.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Thread the beef onto the soaked skewers, leaving a little space between pieces.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the skewers for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until browned with charred edges.
Rest the skewers for 3 minutes before serving with flatbread, lemon wedges or a squeeze of tamarind.

ing: or a very light roast ground coffee
st: Bring [[4 cups]] water to a gentle boil in a small pot.
Add the crushed cardamom pods and saffron and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] ground coffee and return to a gentle simmer, without letting it boil over.
Simmer on very low heat for 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in [[1 tsp]] rosewater.
Let the grounds settle for 2 minutes.
Pour carefully through a fine strainer into small cups or a thermos and serve hot, with dates if you like.
Mix [[2 cups]] flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Add [[0.75 cup]] warm water and [[2 tbsp]] oil and stir until a dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and roll each as thin as you can, until almost see-through.
Heat a large dry skillet or flat griddle over medium-high heat.
Cook one round at a time for 1 to 2 minutes per side until lightly browned and crisp in spots.
Brush lightly with oil if you like, then stack the breads and serve warm or cool.
